claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2023-09-18 reports: Rural coastal Salani had 93% of 88 households on customary land; inland suburban Vaitele had 80% of about 1,300 households on freehold land.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2023-09-18 reports: At Salani, 10/20 participants partly or fully linked inland moves to climate factors (four entirely); storm surge and cyclone rainfall were recurring triggers.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Self-reported attribution within a small qualitative study; tsunami-related and socioeconomic mobility drivers are not all climate hazards.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2023-09-18 reports: At Vaitele, 6/20 households linked movement partly or fully to climate factors; seven participants cited social reasons and seven freehold access, with overlap in environmental changes.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2023-09-18 reports: Seventeen of 20 Salani households near water moved inland; short moves were easier where customary access avoided land-purchase costs.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2019-10-28 reports: UNDP described Salei'a as exposed to sea-level rise, flooding, erosion, stronger tropical storms, rainfall and heat; by 2019 a revetment and raised bridge provided daily access and a disaster escape route.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2017 reports: At Matafa'a, runoff, land management, variable rain, floods and drought were linked to poor water quality and livelihood and health effects; elderly people, women and children bore water-collection burdens.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2017 reports: The report says a mountain gravity-fed system and native reforestation were installed; Matafa'a had water during the three-month September 2011 El Niño drought, with clean water in all homes.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Project-era report of water availability during a drought described by the source as September 2011; neither climate-mode timing nor current scheme operation was independently reverified.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2017 reports: Matafa'a's community-managed scheme set a household maintenance fee; the Independent Water Scheme Association supported filter maintenance and water quality.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-06-30 reports: Women at a Lalomanu workshop said inland relocation reduced sea access and coastal-road customers for craft and seafood businesses.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: The cited passage does not establish whether relocation was climate-, tsunami-, or otherwise driven; no climate-attributed livelihood loss is inferred.

claim_decisions.statement: The Pacific synthesis records Samoa participants' reports of domestic-violence concerns, but explicitly warns that sample/cultural differences may explain the Samoa–Tonga contrast.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: No prevalence denominator, identified relocation trigger or causal climate/mobility effect. Do not generalize this qualitative signal to Samoa as a whole.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-06 reports: In June 2025, PREPARE planned six years of hazard monitoring, early warning, response and urban resilience work, with township planning focused on Sālelologa.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-06 reports: The ESMF identifies Sālelologa land disputes as a potential planning conflict risk; proposed controls map disputes, exclude disputed areas and use consultation and grievance handling.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Preliminary Sālelologa planning safeguard risk around unresolved land disputes, not observed project-induced conflict or a climate-caused incident.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-06 reports: The ESMF flags possible exclusion of women, youth, people with disabilities and other marginalized groups from Sālelologa planning.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Preparation-stage exclusion risk, not proof exclusion occurred or safeguards were delivered.

gaps: Lalomanu relocation accounts do not establish the hazard trigger; tsunami-related movement must not be classified as climate-caused.
Qualitative domestic-violence signals cannot support a countrywide trend or climate-to-violence causal pathway.

executive_assessment.text: Salani and Vaitele show different land-tenure and mobility contexts; Matafa'a and Salei'a provide historical, programme-reported capacity examples.
Lalomanu livelihood trade-offs and caveated protection concerns require careful trigger and sample qualification; PREPARE adds prospective Sālelologa land/inclusion safeguards.
